created_trees.objective: Starting from the fastest correct source 31112, retain its 16-byte SSE2 ASCII-prefix scan and test replacing its scalar suffix with T1's measured 8-byte ASCII-word/mixed-block decoder from 1bef. This tests whether skipping ASCII blocks after the first non-ASCII block helps without sacrificing the faster prefix. Preserve all correctness and protocol constraints; remeasure the combined program and do not assume additive gains.
created_trees.stop_condition: Reject the integration on any correctness failure or if its official mixed-width mean is not faster than 39.98 µs.
created_trees.subject: Test a faster ASCII-prefix scan with a word-scanned scalar suffix

decision.rationale: Lire le snapshot de développement 1b0aac-h04 avant de décider d’une intégration: il est signalé development_valid, mais aucune performance n’est mesurée. Vérifier si son changement apporte une idée distincte à tester sur la meilleure base mesurée.

Use the fastest measured correct source as the integration base. Replace its SSE2 high-bit classification (`_mm_cmpgt_epi8(zero, value)` followed by movemask) with direct `_mm_movemask_epi8(value)`, which extracts the same byte sign bits without the packed comparison. Preserve the existing UTF-8 masks, carry and restricted-byte checks, bounded scalar tail, fallback, and ABI. Do not merge the slower ASCII-prefix or word-scan variants; measure this focused change and retain the base if it does not improve.

The focused movemask integration was correct at 29.611 µs, effectively tied with its 29.620 µs measured base; the earlier combined scan was slower at 56.234 µs. No further evidence-backed integration is likely to improve the candidate reliably. Let the controller select the best verified program and independently confirm it; this is not a claim of confirmed improvement.

children.objective: Primary hypothesis: SIMD masks validate UTF-8 constraints across the whole buffer, unlike T2's ASCII-span locator. Explore block classification, shifted continuation requirements, restricted second-byte checks, cross-block state, and a bounded tail. Compare relevant SIMD variants only when supported by the frozen target and unchanged build; do not alter flags or add runtime environment probing. Keep the supplied scalar implementation as a control, and report any useful hybrid as a distinct variant rather than excluding it. Preserve exact scalar-value validation, ABI, output, and thread budget. Use the official mixed-width n=65536 timing for performance and official ASCII/malformed checks for correctness, paying particular attention to vector boundaries and truncations where covered. Record failed variants.
children.subject: Whole-stream SIMD UTF-8 validation with cross-block state

children.objective: Primary hypothesis: vector high-bit scans can skip ASCII spans while the existing strict scalar decoder handles non-ASCII code points. The benefit depends on the actual official mixed-width input containing useful ASCII spans; do not assume this or use synthetic-only results as evidence for the scored workload. Start decoding at a known code-point boundary and treat the first high-bit byte as input to validate—not as an assumed lead, since it may be a stray continuation. Keep loads and tails within n. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, and thread budget. Measure the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and run the official ASCII/malformed correctness checks, especially for boundaries. Report this approach separately from T1's whole-buffer validation; label any hybrid distinctly and record failed variants.
children.subject: SIMD-assisted ASCII-run skipping with a scalar slow path

children.objective: Primary hypothesis: reducing scalar decoding control flow or dependencies helps the mixed-width workload; the supplied baseline already has an ASCII fast path, so do not assume ASCII scanning is the only scalar cost. Compare the baseline decoder with compact-state/DFA or reduced-branch scalar variants, measuring each under the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and checking official ASCII/malformed correctness. Keep scalar decoding as the focus, but do not treat that focus as a ban on useful correctness-preserving experiments; label any hybrid separately from pure-scalar results. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, bounds, and thread budget. Report failed variants.
children.subject: Branch-reduced scalar UTF-8 decoding

decision.rationale: Lire le snapshot de développement 1b0aac-h04 avant de décider d’une intégration: il est signalé development_valid, mais aucune performance n’est mesurée. Vérifier si son changement apporte une idée distincte à tester sur la meilleure base mesurée.

Use the fastest measured correct source as the integration base. Replace its SSE2 high-bit classification (`_mm_cmpgt_epi8(zero, value)` followed by movemask) with direct `_mm_movemask_epi8(value)`, which extracts the same byte sign bits without the packed comparison. Preserve the existing UTF-8 masks, carry and restricted-byte checks, bounded scalar tail, fallback, and ABI. Do not merge the slower ASCII-prefix or word-scan variants; measure this focused change and retain the base if it does not improve.

The focused movemask integration was correct at 29.611 µs, effectively tied with its 29.620 µs measured base; the earlier combined scan was slower at 56.234 µs. No further evidence-backed integration is likely to improve the candidate reliably. Let the controller select the best verified program and independently confirm it; this is not a claim of confirmed improvement.

children.objective: Primary hypothesis: SIMD masks validate UTF-8 constraints across the whole buffer, unlike T2's ASCII-span locator. Explore block classification, shifted continuation requirements, restricted second-byte checks, cross-block state, and a bounded tail. Compare relevant SIMD variants only when supported by the frozen target and unchanged build; do not alter flags or add runtime environment probing. Keep the supplied scalar implementation as a control, and report any useful hybrid as a distinct variant rather than excluding it. Preserve exact scalar-value validation, ABI, output, and thread budget. Use the official mixed-width n=65536 timing for performance and official ASCII/malformed checks for correctness, paying particular attention to vector boundaries and truncations where covered. Record failed variants.
children.subject: Whole-stream SIMD UTF-8 validation with cross-block state

children.objective: Primary hypothesis: vector high-bit scans can skip ASCII spans while the existing strict scalar decoder handles non-ASCII code points. The benefit depends on the actual official mixed-width input containing useful ASCII spans; do not assume this or use synthetic-only results as evidence for the scored workload. Start decoding at a known code-point boundary and treat the first high-bit byte as input to validate—not as an assumed lead, since it may be a stray continuation. Keep loads and tails within n. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, and thread budget. Measure the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and run the official ASCII/malformed correctness checks, especially for boundaries. Report this approach separately from T1's whole-buffer validation; label any hybrid distinctly and record failed variants.
children.subject: SIMD-assisted ASCII-run skipping with a scalar slow path

children.objective: Primary hypothesis: reducing scalar decoding control flow or dependencies helps the mixed-width workload; the supplied baseline already has an ASCII fast path, so do not assume ASCII scanning is the only scalar cost. Compare the baseline decoder with compact-state/DFA or reduced-branch scalar variants, measuring each under the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and checking official ASCII/malformed correctness. Keep scalar decoding as the focus, but do not treat that focus as a ban on useful correctness-preserving experiments; label any hybrid separately from pure-scalar results. Preserve exact validity, ABI, output, bounds, and thread budget. Report failed variants.
children.subject: Branch-reduced scalar UTF-8 decoding

created_trees.objective: Starting from the fastest correct source 31112, retain its 16-byte SSE2 ASCII-prefix scan and test replacing its scalar suffix with T1's measured 8-byte ASCII-word/mixed-block decoder from 1bef. This tests whether skipping ASCII blocks after the first non-ASCII block helps without sacrificing the faster prefix. Preserve all correctness and protocol constraints; remeasure the combined program and do not assume additive gains.
created_trees.stop_condition: Reject the integration on any correctness failure or if its official mixed-width mean is not faster than 39.98 µs.
